parts.note: OP is the usual abbreviation for opus, a work
to press is to force or push hard

explanation.surface: A despot driving the labour force hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To tyrannise people is to rule them cruelly, keeping them down by harsh treatment: a direct synonym.

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, with the possessive S
day in the sense of an era or period, as in 'in my day'

explanation.surface: Something a father does for fun in his own era, or on Father's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby or recreation pursued in spare hours is exactly a leisure activity.

clue.text: Is taken aback by a fair's attractions

definitions.meaning: read as 'is carried on the back of' a horse or vehicle, as a passenger is
the carousels, waltzers and big wheels at a funfair

explanation.surface: Someone startled by what a funfair has to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' looks like 'surprised', but here it means carried on a back.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger is carried along on a horse's back, and fairground machines are the amusements visitors pay for.

definitions.meaning: an unspecified person, an individual not named
an important person, as in 'he's really a somebody'

explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun names an unidentified individual, and as a noun it means a person of importance.

parts.note: to age is to mature
to pine is to long or yearn for something

explanation.surface: An old pine tree that has survived for many years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the tree, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that endures for ages is everlasting, continuing through a great span of time.

parts.note: not the bird's flight path, but the route food takes when swallowed

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher asking about the migration route of a swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird; it is the act of swallowing.
explanation.definitionFit: The throat passage down which swallowed food travels is the oesophagus or throat.

clue.text: Want to try? Only too willing!

definitions.meaning: an offer: would you like a go, a turn, an attempt
an idiom for doing something eagerly and immediately

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means desiring a go; as an idiom it means instantly and eagerly, without hesitation.

indicators.note: scattered about, so the letters of the cult members' name are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Objectionable members of the Unification Church being broken up and sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moonies' are members of the Unification Church; 'dispersed' shuffles its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpleasant or disgusting, especially a smell, is described this way: a synonym.

parts.note: a soldier captured during combat, read not as a brawler arrested by police

explanation.surface: A man arrested for brawling.
explanation.definitionFit: A combatant taken captive by the enemy during hostilities is held as a POW.

clue.text: Employed you and me — and another chap

parts.note: us is the pronoun for you and me together
Ed is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A firm that took on the two of us plus one more man.
explanation.definitionFit: Something employed has been put to work or utilised: a past-participle synonym.

clue.text: Much improved, so enjoying greater popularity

definitions.meaning: the idiom for 'that's better', said of something nearer what is wanted
read literally: further people are fond of the thing

explanation.surface: A product that, being much better, now sells more.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something being better, and literally says that additional people are fond of it.

clue.text: Failure in providing returns as a company

indicators.note: turns back, so the word for providing is read backwards

parts.note: providing in the sense of 'on condition that', which is if

explanation.surface: A firm's poor returns signalling the business has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' looks like financial profit, but it signals reading IF backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A humiliating flop or complete disaster is called a fiasco: a direct synonym.

clue.text: She hurried round to a furniture designer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ran goes round the word to, encircling it

parts.note: to hurry is to run, past tense ran
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman rushing about to reach a famous cabinet-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English furniture designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was a celebrated English cabinet-maker whose name labels a furniture style.

clue.text: We shall shortly be having gin cocktail — here's health!

parts.note: we shall shortened to the contraction we'll, apostrophe ignored
taken as written

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A toast before gin cocktails: 'Here's health!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here's health!' is a drinking toast; the definition is 'health'.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of being healthy, comfortable and happy is a close synonym of good health.

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild bear that someone set free.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone set free from captivity or restraint has been released or emancipated: a synonym.

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A demand for total silence at all times.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer folly or sheer luck means complete, utter, unmitigated: an adjective synonym.

clue.text: They're not striking examples of comradeship

definitions.text: They're not striking examples of comradeship

parts.words: They're not striking examples of comradeship
parts.note: striking as in going on strike: strikebreakers do not stand with their workmates

explanation.surface: People who are poor models of friendship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' seems to mean remarkable, but it means taking industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who break a strike are derided by union members as traitors to solidarity.

clue.text: Tom joins chap of Spanish origin

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
Alan is a man's name

explanation.surface: Tom meeting a man whose family came from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalonia is a region of Spain, so someone or something from there has Spanish origins.

indicators.note: mid- means the centre, so take the central letter of the word off

parts.note: rightful means fair or just

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at mid-off simply playing awfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-off is a cricket fielding position; here it gives the middle letter of 'off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreadful or appalling is called frightful: a straightforward synonym.

parts.note: gall is bitterness or rancour
an eon is an age, a vast period of time

explanation.surface: Resentment linked to an ancient trade or skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a skill; it is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sailing ship of the 15th to 18th centuries is an old type of vessel.

indicators.note: breaking something shatters it, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A shop opening up during the lunch break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lunch break' reads as a meal pause; 'break' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a gate or door's catch is to open it: a verb synonym.

clue.text: To be consistent, he must be in the middle

indicators.note: he has to be placed inside the word for the middle

parts.note: the core is the middle of something

explanation.surface: Advice that for consistency a man should stay centrist.
explanation.definitionFit: Arguments that hang together logically are consistent; the verb means to stick together.

parts.note: the main performer is the star
a swell is an old word for a fashionable gentleman, a toff

explanation.surface: A sea swell setting a ship in motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' and 'swell' suggest the sea; here they are a star and a toff.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out or get going is to begin moving: a phrasal-verb synonym.

definitions.meaning: a person's nearest pub is called their local

explanation.surface: Residents of the area around some pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain one's local is the nearby pub one habitually drinks in.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of an area are its natives, and in British usage nearby bars are each someone's regular haunt.

clue.text: It may be cut and pickled

definitions.text: It may be cut and pickled

parts.words: It may be cut and pickled
parts.note: one cuts a dance step, a skip, and pickles the flower bud used in cooking

explanation.surface: Something like a vegetable sliced and preserved in vinegar.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'cut a caper' is to dance playfully; capers are pickled flower buds.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a frolicsome leap and the pickled bud of a Mediterranean shrub.

clue.text: Not mad about silver? It's very much in fashion

indicators.note: the phrase for sane goes about, around, the chemical symbol

parts.note: all there is an idiom for sane, in full possession of one's faculties
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone sanely enthusiastic about silver, now a fashionable metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something hugely popular and fashionable at present.

parts.note: not moving at a traffic light, but a golf stroke played on the ... green

explanation.surface: A driver asking whether to move off at a green light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on green' suggests traffic lights; the green is in golf, and 'go' a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle golf stroke made on the putting surface to roll the ball into the hole.

clue.text: I'd eat no differently, though trying to lose weight

indicators.note: in a different way, so these letters are arranged in a different order

explanation.surface: A slimmer insisting their eating habits haven't changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restricting food intake to slim down is following a regime of eating less.

clue.text: Chief required in some lawless state

indicators.note: the word for chief goes inside the word for some

parts.note: any means some, as in 'have you any?'
arch means chief or principal, as in archbishop

explanation.surface: A country without law needing a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition with no government or order is a state without law: a synonym.
